correctness.rationale: For every one of the 256 Wolfram binary radius-one local maps, finite input-block realizability agrees exactly with paths in its labeled four-pair-state de Bruijn graph. The deterministic nonempty subset construction accepts and counts every output word exactly once. All its nonempty states are accessible and accepting, so the spatial word growth equals the nonnegative integer adjacency-matrix Perron root. The saved exact checker derives 256 characteristic polynomials, isolates their largest positive zeros into 19 pairwise-disjoint rational intervals using exact Sturm counts, verifies a common irreducible factor within each class, reproduces both tabulations byte-for-byte, and independently checks all 2304 finite output-block counts at lengths 0 through 8. The unrestricted limit follows from Perron-Frobenius theory, not bounded experiments.

value.rationale: The entire 256-rule family is a standard finite laboratory for symbolic dynamics, and one-step spatial image entropy measures precisely how many configurations remain reachable after one local update. The classification exhibits only 19 exact logarithms of algebraic roots, classifies the 30 surjective and 2 zero-entropy cases, and gives the sharp maximum for all 226 nonsurjective images with exactly four maximizers and a distinct four-rule runner-up. This is a complete natural invariant and structural extremal distinction, not an arbitrary hand-picked rule/length or numerical approximation. It does not claim a universal theorem for higher-radius cellular automata.
